headline: Congo’s Ebola outbreak has more than doubled in three months, the WHO says
summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo now has more than 11,000 confirmed cases. As of 15 November, Congo had reported 11,376 confirmed cases and 5,568 deaths, according to the EU’s disease agency, ECDC.
why: It is one of the largest Ebola outbreaks on record. The Bundibugyo virus behind it has no known vaccine or treatment, and violence in the worst-hit provinces makes it harder to contain.

event.t: WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on 17 November that cases have more than doubled in three months. The outbreak has reached eight of Congo’s 26 provinces.
ECDC counts 11,376 confirmed cases and 5,568 deaths in Congo, based on data up to 14 November. About half of confirmed cases have died.
Tedros said children make up more than a quarter of confirmed cases and a third of deaths.
There is no known vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo virus. Cases linked to the outbreak were also reported in Kenya and Nigeria in October, ECDC says.
